source.title: Mod-p Poincaré Duality in p-adic analytic geometry
readSections: arXiv 2111.01830v3 (21 February 2024, 'Major revision'), read in full: 101 pages, SHA-256 a984d973782649972a835b302e20ec91fc9c1abc5e5b43c7eccc5934b9c2c951, fetched from https://arxiv.org/pdf/2111.01830v3 on 23 September 2026 (v1: 2 November 2021; v2: 25 August 2022). Item locators are v3's pages. The Annals article (received 12 June 2022, revised 31 January 2024, accepted 18 June 2024, published online 29 April 2025) is not freely available; v3 postdates the revision and the paper's own Remark 3.5.6 records the referee-requested restriction to nice models, so v3 is taken as the accepted text. Every recorded mistake was checked on v3's page images.

Read: §1 (Theorems 1.1.1–1.1.4, Remark 1.1.5, the plan of proof §1.2, conventions §1.4), §2 (Definition 2.1.1 to Lemma 2.7.9), §3 (§3.1 to Lemma 3.6.6), §4 (Definition 4.1.1 to Theorem 4.4.24), §5 (Theorem 5.1.1 to Theorem 5.5.6), Appendices A (Definition A.1 to Lemma A.19), B (Lemma B.1 to Corollary B.15), C (Definition C.1 to Lemma C.9), D (Definition D.1 to Lemma D.13) and the references.

Cited inputs were not read; items resting on Zavyalov [Zav21a], [Zav21b], [Zav21c], Scholze [Sch13a], [Sch13b], Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze [BMS18], Bhatt [Bha19], Berkovich [Ber93], Huber [Hub96], Bosch–Lütkebohmert–Raynaud [BLR95], Temkin [Tem00], [Tem17], Elkik [Elk73], Česnavičius–Koshikawa [ČK19], Fujiwara–Kato [FK18], Gabber–Ramero [GR03], [GR18], Conrad [Con99], Fontaine [Fon82] and the Stacks Project state them as the paper uses them.

summary: Zavyalov proves Poincaré duality for F_p-étale cohomology of a smooth proper rigid-analytic space X of pure dimension d over a non-archimedean field K of mixed characteristic (0, p) (Theorem 1.1.4 = 5.4.4): the Galois-equivariant trace H^{2d}(X_K̂̄, F_p(d)) → F_p makes the cup-product pairing perfect in every degree, answering Scholze's question and completing Huber's and Berkovich's ℓ ≠ p theorem; versions for F_p-local systems and Z/p^n, Z_p, Q_p coefficients follow. By the primitive comparison it suffices to prove almost duality for RΓ(X, O^+/p) (Theorem 5.1.1). On a formal model 𝔛 with reduced special fibre he builds Faltings' trace Rν_∗(O^{+,a}/p) → ω^{•,a}_{𝔛_0}(−d)[−2d], gluing a BMS-type map on the smooth locus with Scholze's Ω^d(−d) ≅ R^dµ_∗Ô on the generic fibre through a Hartogs property of the dualizing sheaf; local almost duality (Theorem 4.4.24) is proved on polystable models by continuous cohomology of Z_p(1)^d and descended through rig-isomorphisms and finite quotients using his local altered uniformization; almost Grothendieck duality on 𝔛_0 globalizes it. The new theory goes to a proposed Part II of Huber's classical analytic cohomology roadmap; Grothendieck duality for universally coherent schemes to the pending six-functor roadmap's coherent layer AS.1, finitely presented compactifications to L2, reduced-fibre facts to AdicSpacesPartII, Berkovich's trace and the étale Huber–Berkovich comparison to H3, the category comparison to TB.0, Scholze's comparison theorems to P8 and Fontaine's and Bhatt's twist computations to AI.0. Twelve misprints are recorded.

items.name: Theorem 1.1.2 (Poincaré duality for smooth proper varieties, SGA 4 XVIII 3.2.5)
items.statement: For X smooth proper of pure dimension d over a field k and ℓ ≠ char k, there is a Galois-equivariant trace H^{2d}(X_k̄, F_ℓ(d)) → F_ℓ for which the cup-product pairing H^i(X_k̄, F_ℓ) ⊗ H^{2d−i}(X_k̄, F_ℓ(d)) → F_ℓ is perfect for all i.
items.note: Quoted as the model statement; EDC.2:pairings plans the perfect pairings for smooth proper schemes.

items.name: Theorem 1.1.3 (Huber, Berkovich: ℓ-adic Poincaré duality for smooth proper rigid spaces)
items.statement: Let X be a smooth proper rigid-analytic space of pure dimension d over a non-archimedean field K and ℓ a prime invertible in O_K. There is a Galois-equivariant trace t_X : H^{2d}(X_K̂̄, F_ℓ(d)) → F_ℓ such that H^i(X_K̂̄, F_ℓ) ⊗ H^{2d−i}(X_K̂̄, F_ℓ(d)) → F_ℓ is perfect for all i ≥ 0.
items.note: Cited from Huber [Hub96, Theorem 7.5.3] and Berkovich [Ber93, Theorem 7.3.1]. H3 plans Hub96 7.2.2/7.5.3 only for smooth analytic curves, as ECD 24.1 needs; the paper stresses that ℓ must be invertible in O_K (ℓ ≠ p in mixed characteristic), unlike Theorem 1.1.2.

items.name: Remark 1.1.5 (no duality at ℓ = char K)
items.statement: For a proper rigid-analytic K-space X of dimension > 0 and ℓ = char K, H^{2d}(X_K̂̄, F_ℓ) = 0, so Poincaré duality cannot hold; Theorems 1.1.3 and 1.1.4 together cover every prime ℓ ≠ char K.
items.note: Stated without proof (Artin–Schreier). It fixes the scope of the Part II's final theorem.

items.name: Rigid-analytic spaces as adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(K, O_K)
items.statement: A rigid-analytic K-space is an adic space locally of finite type over Spa(K, O_K) [Hub94, §4, Prop. 4.5]; admissible formal O_K-schemes are flat, topologically finitely presented formal O_K-schemes, with fibres 𝔛_i = 𝔛 mod ϖ^{i+1} and generic fibre 𝔛_K.
items.note: AdicEtaleGeometry A2 plans classical analytic geometry inside adic spaces; AdicSpacesPartII R2 plans admissible formal schemes and the generic-fibre functor.

items.name: The pro-étale site and the completed structure sheaves Ô^+_X, Ô_X
items.statement: The (κ-small) pro-étale site X_proét of a rigid space [Sch13a, Sch16], Ô^+_X = lim O^+_X/p^n and Ô_X = Ô^+_X[1/p], with the morphisms λ : (X_proét, Ô^+) → (X_ét, O^+), t : (X_ét, O^+) → (𝔛, O_𝔛) and ν = t ∘ λ (the paper's ν differs from [Sch13a]'s); RΓ(X_C, Z_p) := RΓ_proét(X_C, Ẑ_p).
items.note: A1 plans the pro-étale site with Scholze's corrected coverings; AI.3 plans the completed integral structure sheaf.

items.name: Almost mathematics over O_C and the almost derived category
items.statement: Almost mathematics with respect to the flat idempotent ideal 𝔪 ⊂ O_C: almost zero and almost isomorphic modules, the categories Mod^a and D(X)^a (the Verdier quotient by complexes with almost zero cohomology), and the functor (−)_! [GR03, Zav21a].
items.note: P0 plans almost-zero modules, the Serre quotient, almostification and its adjoints for an abstract idempotent base ideal.

items.name: Perfect and almost perfect pairings
items.statement: In a closed symmetric monoidal category, a pairing A ⊗ B → 1 is perfect if the induced A → Hom(B, 1) and B → Hom(A, 1) are isomorphisms; over O_C (or on 𝔛) a pairing is almost perfect if the induced maps to RalHom are isomorphisms in the almost derived category.
items.note: Used as the form of every duality statement in §§4–5.

items.name: The Breuil–Kisin twist O_C{1} and dlog
items.statement: O_C{1} := T_p(Ω^1_{O_C/Z_p}) = L̂_{O_C/Z_p}[−1] [BMS18, Def. 8.2], with dlog : Z_p(1) → O_C{1} induced by µ_{p^∞} → Ω^1_{O_C/Z_p}, f ↦ df/f; O_C{n} = O_C{1}^{⊗n}.
items.note: AI.0 plans Breuil–Kisin twists, distinguishing A_inf{1}, its étale Z_p(1) realization and the reduction twist.

items.name: Definition 2.1.1 (the category of finitely presented compactifications)
items.statement: For a separated finitely presented morphism f : X → Y of qcqs schemes, Comp_fp(X/Y) has objects the open immersions j : X → X̄ over Y with X̄ → Y proper and finitely presented, and morphisms the Y-maps of compactifications; a morphism is strict if it is an isomorphism over X in the appropriate sense ([Stacks 0ATT], Remarks 2.1.2–2.1.3: pullback preserves strictness).
items.note: The finitely presented variant of the Stacks Project's category of compactifications.

items.name: Lemma 2.1.4 (compactifications over a limit of bases)
items.statement: If Y = lim Y_i is a cofiltered limit of qcqs schemes with affine transition maps and X_0 → Y_0 is separated of finite presentation, then colim_i Comp_fp(X_0 ×_{Y_0} Y_i/Y_i) → Comp_fp(X_0 ×_{Y_0} Y/Y) is an equivalence.
items.note: Noetherian approximation of compactifications.

items.name: Corollary 2.1.5 (Nagata: Comp_fp(X/Y) is nonempty and cofiltered)
items.statement: For Y qcqs and f : X → Y separated of finite presentation, Comp_fp(X/Y) is nonempty and cofiltered, and can be computed using strict morphisms.
items.note: Nonemptiness is the finitely presented Nagata theorem, by noetherian approximation ([Stacks 01ZA, 01ZM, 0ATU]); L2 plans the nonnoetherian Nagata statement, and the cofilteredness with strict morphisms is the added adapter that the upper-shriek construction of §2.2 needs.

items.name: Definition 2.2.1 (universally coherent schemes) and FPS_S
items.statement: A scheme S is universally coherent if every finitely presented S-scheme is coherent. For S qcqs universally coherent, FPS_S is the category of separated finitely presented S-schemes; every morphism in it is pseudo-coherent, it is perfect if and only if of finite Tor dimension, and F ∈ D_qcoh(X) is pseudo-coherent if and only if F ∈ D^−_coh(X).
items.note: Extends the noetherian setting of the Stacks Project's duality chapter [Stacks 0DWE]; §§2.3–2.4 apply it over a rank-one valuation ring O_K and over O_K/ϖ^{n+1}.

items.name: Theorem 2.2.2 (Kiehl, Fujiwara–Kato: proper pushforward preserves coherence)
items.statement: For a proper morphism f : X → Y in FPS_S, Rf_* maps D^∗_coh(X) to D^∗_coh(Y) for ∗ ∈ {∅, +, −, b}.
items.note: Cited from [FK18, Corollary I.8.1.4] and [Kie72, Theorem 2.9]; it replaces the noetherian hypothesis of [Stacks 0A9P].

items.name: Theorem 2.2.3 (the upper-shriek pseudo-functor on FPS_S)
items.statement: There is a pseudo-functor (−)^! : FPS_S → Cat with X^! = D^+_qc(X), f^! ≅ Lf^∗ for an open immersion f, and f^! right adjoint to Rf_∗ : D^+_qc(X) → D^+_qc(Y) for a proper f.
items.note: The proof adapts [Stacks 0DWE]/[0A9Y] with finitely presented compactifications (Corollary 2.1.5) and open base change via Theorem 2.2.2. The statement prints 'FPS_R' for FPS_S (sourceIssues E1).

items.name: Lemma 2.2.4 (flat base change for f^!)
items.statement: For a cartesian square in FPS_S with g flat there is a canonical isomorphism Lg′^∗ ∘ f^! ≅ f′^! ∘ Lg^∗.
items.note: As [Stacks 0E9U], with Theorem 2.2.2 replacing the noetherian hypothesis.

items.name: Lemma 2.2.5 (f^! of a perfect morphism)
items.statement: For a perfect morphism f : X → Y in FPS_S there is a canonical isomorphism µ_{K,f} : Lf^∗K ⊗^L f^!O_Y → f^!K for K ∈ D^+_qc(Y).
items.note: Constructed as in [Stacks 0B6T]; reduce to perfect closed immersions and P^1_Y.

items.name: Lemma 2.2.6 (f^! of affine and projective space)
items.statement: For f : A^d_Y → Y, f^!O_Y ≅ O_{A^d}[d]; for P^d_Y → Y, f^!O_Y ≅ O(−d−1)[d].

items.name: Lemma 2.2.7 (boundedness and coherence of f^!)
items.statement: For f : X → Y in FPS_S: (1) f^! sends D^+_coh(Y) to D^+_coh(X); (2) if f has finite Tor dimension, f^! sends D^b_coh(Y) to D^b_coh(X); (3) if f is flat, f^!O_Y is Y-perfect [Stacks 0DI0].
items.note: Part (2) is printed with the categories reversed (sourceIssues E2).

items.name: Construction 2.2.8 and Lemma 2.2.9 (the relative dualizing complex)
items.statement: For flat f : X → S in FPS_S, a map ξ : ∆_∗O_X → Lp_1^∗f^!O_S on X ×_S X, and (f^!O_S, ξ) is a relative dualizing complex in the sense of [Stacks 0E2T].

items.name: Corollary 2.2.10 (base change of the relative dualizing complex)
items.statement: For f : X → S flat in FPS_S and any g : S′ → S in FPS_S, there is a canonical base change isomorphism β_g : Lg′^∗f^!O_S ≅ f′^!O_{S′}, compatible with composition.
items.note: From uniqueness of relative dualizing complexes [Stacks 0E2Y].

items.name: Lemma 2.2.11 (smooth morphisms)
items.statement: For f : X → S smooth of pure relative dimension d there is a canonical isomorphism α_f : f^!O_S ≅ Ω^d_{X/S}[d], compatible with the base change maps β_g.

items.name: Corollary 2.2.12 (étale morphisms)
items.statement: For étale f in FPS_S there is a canonical isomorphism f^! ≅ Lf^∗.

items.name: Lemma 2.2.13 (amplitude of the dualizing complex)
items.statement: If f : X → S is flat, finitely presented and separated with fibres of dimension ≤ d, then f^!O_S ∈ D^{[−d,0]}_coh(X) and has Tor amplitude [−d, 0] over S.

items.name: Definition 2.2.14 (dualizing complex and dualizing module)
items.statement: For X → S flat, finitely presented, separated of pure relative dimension d: ω^•_{X/S} := f^!O_S and ω_{X/S} := H^{−d}(ω^•_{X/S}).

items.name: Traces of finite morphisms and Lemma 2.2.16
items.statement: For a finite morphism f : X → Y between quasi-compact smooth separated S-schemes of pure relative dimension d, the trace Tr_f : f_∗Ω^d_{X/S} → Ω^d_{Y/S} from Lemma 2.2.11 and the (Rf_∗, f^!)-adjunction; for finite locally free f, Tr_f : f_∗O_X → O_Y glued from Tr_{B/A} ([Stacks 0BVH]). Lemma 2.2.16: for finite flat f : X → Y between quasi-compact smooth separated S-schemes of pure relative dimension d, the Grothendieck trace composed with f_∗f^∗Ω^d_{Y/S} → f_∗Ω^d_{X/S} equals Tr_f ⊗ id under the projection formula.
items.note: [NS19, Theorem 9.2.14(i)] or [Con00, (2.7.41)] for noetherian S, then approximation ([Stacks 01YT, 0B6J]).

items.name: Definition 2.3.1 (depth via local cohomology) and weakly associated points
items.statement: For a coherent sheaf F on a scheme with noetherian underlying space, the depth δ_X(x, F) of F at x is defined through local cohomology as in [GR18, (10.4.19)]; weakly associated points are those of depth 0 (Lemma 2.3.3).
items.note: The nonnoetherian depth theory of Gabber–Ramero.

items.name: Lemma 2.3.4 (weakly associated primes of torsion-free modules)
items.statement: If R is reduced with |Spec R| noetherian and M is a torsion-free R-module, every weakly associated prime of M is minimal.
items.note: Via [Stacks 05C3] and prime avoidance.

items.name: Lemma 2.3.5 (flatness of the dualizing module)
items.statement: For X separated, flat and finitely presented over a rank-one valuation ring O_K, of pure relative dimension d, ω_X is O_K-flat.

items.name: Lemma 2.3.6 (torsion-freeness over a field)
items.statement: For a field k and X separated of finite type over k of pure dimension d, ω_X is torsion-free.

items.name: Theorem 2.3.7 (reflexivity of the dualizing module)
items.statement: Let X be a separated flat finitely presented O_K-scheme of pure relative dimension d with smooth generic fibre and geometrically reduced special fibre. Then ω_X is a reflexive coherent O_X-module.
items.note: The analogue of reflexivity of dualizing sheaves on normal schemes; proved by depth estimates ([GR18, Cor. 10.4.46], [Stacks 05AP]).

items.name: Definition 2.4.1 (dualizing complex of an admissible formal scheme)
items.statement: For a separated admissible formal O_K-scheme 𝔛 of pure dimension d, ω^•_𝔛 := R lim ω^•_{𝔛_n} (the mod ϖ^{n+1} fibres over O_K/ϖ^{n+1}) and ω_𝔛 := lim ω_{𝔛_n}; it is defined up to non-unique isomorphism (Warning 2.4.2).

items.name: Theorem 2.4.4 (properties of ω^•_𝔛)
items.statement: For 𝔛 separated admissible of pure dimension d: (1) ω^•_𝔛 ∈ D^{[−d,0]}_coh(𝔛) and ω^•_𝔛 ⊗^L O_{𝔛_n} ≅ ω^•_{𝔛_n}; (2) H^{−d}(ω^•_𝔛) ≅ ω_𝔛 is coherent; (3) on the smooth locus there is a canonical isomorphism r_{𝔛^sm} : Ω̂^d_{𝔛^sm}[d] ≅ ω^•_{𝔛^sm}, whence Ω̂^d ≅ ω_𝔛|_{𝔛^sm}.
items.note: Via [Stacks 0BCB, 0D60], [FK18, I.3.2.1] and [Zav21a, Lemma 4.8.13].

items.name: Corollary 2.4.5 (O_K-flatness of ω_𝔛)
items.statement: For 𝔛 as in Theorem 2.4.4, ω_𝔛 is O_K-flat.

items.name: Lemma 2.4.6 (bounded coherent complexes are derived complete)
items.statement: Every F ∈ D^b_coh(𝔛) is derived ϖ-complete.
items.note: Via [Stacks 0999].

items.name: Lemma 2.4.7 (étale pullback of ω)
items.statement: For an étale morphism f : 𝔛 → 𝔜 of separated admissible formal O_K-schemes there is a (non-canonical) isomorphism Lf^∗ω^•_𝔜 ≅ ω^•_𝔛 and a canonical isomorphism f^∗ω_𝔜 ≅ ω_𝔛 when both have pure dimension d.

items.name: Lemma 2.4.8 and Corollary 2.4.9 (completion of algebraic models)
items.statement: For X flat finitely presented over O_K with completion c : X̂ → X and F ∈ D^b_coh(X), Lc^∗F ≅ R lim Li′_n^∗F; hence Lc^∗ω^•_X ≅ ω^•_{X̂} and there is a canonical isomorphism c^∗ω_X ≅ ω_{X̂}.

items.name: Definition 2.5.1 (sections extending from a dense open and the generic fibre)
items.statement: For a coherent F on 𝔛 and an open 𝔘, j_{𝔘,∗}(F|_𝔘) ∩ F_K is the kernel of j_{X_K,∗}F_K ⊕ j_{𝔘,∗}F|_𝔘 → j_{𝔘_K,∗}(F|_𝔘)_K.

items.name: Lemmas 2.5.3–2.5.4 (Hartogs-type extension)
items.statement: If 𝔛 has reduced special fibre and 𝔘 ⊂ 𝔛 is dense open: (2.5.3) for a vector bundle E, E → j_{𝔘,∗}E|_𝔘 is injective; (2.5.4) for a reflexive coherent F, F ≅ j_{𝔘,∗}(F|_𝔘) ∩ F_K.
items.note: Via [Con99, Lemma 2.1.4], Lemmas B.6 and B.12.

items.name: Theorem 2.5.5 (reflexivity and Hartogs extension for ω_𝔛)
items.statement: Let 𝔛 be separated admissible of pure dimension d with smooth generic fibre and geometrically reduced special fibre. Then (1) ω_𝔛 is reflexive coherent; (2) ω_𝔛 ≅ j_{𝔘,∗}(ω_𝔛|_𝔘) ∩ (ω_𝔛)_K for every dense open 𝔘 ⊂ 𝔛.
items.note: From Elkik's algebraization (Lemma B.5), Corollary 2.4.9, Theorem 2.3.7 and flatness of completion. This is the device used to define Faltings' trace from the smooth locus and the generic fibre (§1.2, (1.3)).

items.name: Lemmas 2.6.1–2.6.2 (trace of a proper morphism of formal models)
items.statement: For a proper morphism f : 𝔛 → 𝔜 of separated admissible formal O_K-schemes of the same pure dimension d there is a unique Tr_f : f_∗ω_𝔛 → ω_𝔜 compatible with H^{−d} of the Grothendieck traces of the f_n; Tr_{g∘f} = Tr_g ∘ g_∗Tr_f.
items.note: Via [Stacks 0B6J].

items.name: Theorem 2.7.1 (Bosch–Lütkebohmert–Raynaud: formal models with reduced special fibre)
items.statement: For K algebraically closed, the generic fibre functor induces an equivalence between admissible formal O_K-schemes with reduced special fibre, localized at rig-isomorphisms, and qcqs reduced rigid K-spaces.
items.note: From Raynaud's theorem [BL93, Theorem 4.1], Lemma B.7 and the Reduced Fibre Theorem B.9. R2 plans the Raynaud generic-fibre functor and admissible blow-ups, not this reduced-fibre localization.

items.name: Lemma 2.7.3 (Ω^d of the generic fibre is the generic fibre of ω)
items.statement: For 𝔛 separated admissible with smooth generic fibre X_K of pure dimension d and geometrically reduced special fibre, there is a canonical isomorphism s_𝔛 : Ω^d_{X_K} ≅ (ω_𝔛)_K extending the generic fibre of r_{𝔛^sm}; indeed Ω^d_X[d] ≅ (ω^•_𝔛)_K (Remark 2.7.4).
items.note: Elkik algebraization, Corollaries 2.2.10, 2.4.9 and Lemma 2.2.11; the proof names two steps 'the third' (sourceIssues E3).

items.name: Lemma 2.7.5 (compatibility of s_𝔛 with morphisms of models)
items.statement: For a morphism f : 𝔛′ → 𝔛 of admissible models of X with geometrically reduced special fibres, s_𝔛 = (Tr_f)_K ∘ s_{𝔛′}, where (Tr_f)_K uses the base change isomorphism α_{𝔛′,𝔛} of Lemma C.8.
items.note: Via Corollary B.15.

items.name: Theorem/Definition 2.7.6 (coherent trace for proper smooth rigid spaces)
items.statement: For a proper morphism f : X → Y of qcqs separated smooth rigid K-spaces of pure dimension d there is a unique Tr_f : f_∗Ω^d_X → Ω^d_Y such that (Tr_𝔣)_K ∘ f_∗(s_𝔛) = s_𝔜 ∘ Tr_f for every model 𝔣 : 𝔛 → 𝔜 of f with geometrically reduced special fibres.
items.note: Existence by Theorem 2.7.1, Lemmas 2.7.5 and 2.6.2.

items.name: Definition 2.7.7 (explicit trace of a finite étale morphism)
items.statement: For finite étale f : X → Y of smooth rigid spaces of pure dimension d, Tr^expl_f := Tr_f ⊗ id : f_∗Ω^d_X ≅ f_∗O_X ⊗ Ω^d_Y → Ω^d_Y, with Tr_f : f_∗O_X → O_Y glued from Tr_{B/A}; similarly for finite flat morphisms of formal schemes (Remark 2.7.8).
items.note: R3 plans the trace of finite locally free algebras and finite étale analytic maps.

items.name: Lemma 2.7.9 (the two traces agree)
items.statement: For finite étale f as above, Tr_f = Tr^expl_f.
items.note: Reduce to a finite locally free smooth model ([BGR84, 6.4.1/5], Corollaries B.8, B.14) and apply Lemma 2.2.16. The proof swaps A′ and B′ (sourceIssues E4).

items.name: Definition 3.2.1 (R̃^nν_∗Ô^+)
items.statement: For an admissible formal O_C-scheme 𝔛 with generic fibre X, R̃^nν_∗Ô^+_X := R^nν_∗Ô^+_X / (R^nν_∗Ô^+_X)[(ζ_p − 1)^∞] (= modulo p^∞-torsion).

items.name: Lemma 3.2.2 (cup products descend to wedge powers)
items.statement: There is a unique O_𝔛-linear ∪^n : ∧^n R̃^1ν_∗Ô^+ → R̃^nν_∗Ô^+ compatible with the cup product on tensor powers.
items.note: Anti-commutativity [Stacks 0FP5]; for p = 2 use that R̃^n is 2-torsion-free.

items.name: Bhatt: cotangent complexes of O_C and of perfectoids
items.statement: L̂_{O_C/Z_p} ≅ O_C{1}[1] is free of rank one in degree −1 [Bha19, Remark 3.19], and L̂_{Ô^+_X/O_C} ≅ 0 on X_proét since Ô^+ is perfectoid [Bha19, Corollary 3.28], so L̂_{Ô^+/Z_p} ≅ Ô^+{1}[1].
items.note: Cited from Bhatt's Arizona notes. DD.0 plans the cotangent complex; the perfectoid vanishing and the computation for O_C are the inputs behind the Breuil–Kisin twist that AI.0 constructs.

items.name: Lemmas 3.2.3–3.2.4 (H^0 of the completed cotangent complexes)
items.note: Via the transitivity triangles, [GR03, 7.2.8] and [BMS18, Remark 5.5].

items.name: Definition 3.2.5 (the BMS maps Φ^n_𝔛 for general admissible 𝔛)
items.statement: Φ′^1_𝔛 := H^0(Φ′_𝔛){−1} : Ω̂^1_𝔛{−1} → R^1ν_∗Ô^+, where Φ′_𝔛 : L̂_{O_𝔛/Z_p} → Rν_∗L̂_{Ô^+/Z_p}; Φ^1_𝔛 its composite to R̃^1, and Φ^n_𝔛 := ∪^n ∘ ∧^nΦ^1_𝔛 : Ω̂^n_𝔛{−n} → R̃^nν_∗Ô^+_X. These are functorial for flat morphisms, étale local (Remarks 3.2.6–3.2.7) and satisfy Künneth for Ĝ_m^d (Remark 3.2.8).
items.note: [BMS18] define these maps for smooth 𝔛 only.

items.name: Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze, Theorem 8.3 (Hodge–Tate cohomology sheaves of Ω̃)
items.statement: For smooth 𝔛 over O_C, Ω̃_𝔛 := Lη_{ζ_p−1}Rν_∗Ô^+_X has cohomology sheaves H^i(Ω̃_𝔛) ≅ Ω̂^i_𝔛{−i}, compatibly with products.
items.note: AI.4 plans the Hodge–Tate specialization of AΩ identifying its cohomology sheaves with differential forms and Breuil–Kisin twists.

items.name: The décalage operator Lη_f and its cohomology formula
items.statement: For a nonzerodivisor f, Lη_f on the derived category with H^i(Lη_fK) ≅ H^i(K)/H^i(K)[f] ⊗ f^i, and the criteria of [BMS18, Lemma 6.4, Corollary 6.5, Proposition 6.7, Lemmas 6.10, 8.11(ii)] (almost isomorphisms become isomorphisms after Lη when cohomology has no 𝔪-torsion).
items.note: AI.1 plans Lη_f, its cohomology formula, lax monoidality and the completion statements.

items.name: Lemma 3.3.1 (smooth models: R^nν_∗Ô^+ modulo torsion)
items.statement: For smooth 𝔛, R^nν_∗Ô^+/(ζ_p − 1)-torsion is finite locally free and equals R̃^nν_∗Ô^+.
items.note: From [BMS18, Theorem 8.3, Lemma 6.4].

items.name: Lemma 3.3.2 (smooth models: the image of Φ^n)
items.statement: For smooth 𝔛, Φ^n_𝔛 is an isomorphism onto (ζ_p − 1)^n R̃^nν_∗Ô^+.
items.note: From [BMS18, Lemma 6.10, Theorem 8.3, 8.7, Proposition 6.7, Corollary 8.13(ii)].

items.name: Theorem 3.3.3 (Fontaine: the image of dlog)
items.statement: O_C{1} is free of rank one and the O_C-linearization dlog : O_C(1) → O_C{1} is injective with image (ζ_p − 1)O_C{1}, for any primitive p-th root of unity ζ_p; hence 0 → Ω̂^n{−n} → Ω̂^n(−n) → Q → 0 with image (ζ_p − 1)^n.
items.note: Fontaine's theorem ([Fon82, Theorem 1], [Bei12, §1.3], [SZ18, Theorem 3.1]), reproved via C_p and L̂_{O_C/O_{C_p}} = 0.

items.name: Theorem/Definition 3.3.4 and Definition 3.3.5 (Ψ′^n and Ψ^d on smooth models)
items.statement: For smooth 𝔛 there is a unique isomorphism Ψ′^n_𝔛 : R̃^nν_∗Ô^+ ≅ Ω̂^n_𝔛(−n) with Ψ′^n ∘ (ζ_p − 1)^n = ι_n ∘ (Φ^n)^{−1}; Ψ^d_𝔛 is the composite R^dν_∗Ô^+ → R̃^d → Ω̂^d(−d) → ω_𝔛(−d) (via r_𝔛).

items.name: Scholze: Ω^1(−1) ≅ R^1µ_∗Ô and its exterior powers
items.statement: For smooth X over C, Sch′^1_X : Ω^1_{X_ét} ≅ R^1λ_∗Ô_X(1) ([Sch13a, Corollary 6.19, Remark 6.20], [Sch13b, Lemma 3.24]), giving Sch^1_X : Ω^1_X(−1) ≅ R^1µ_∗Ô_X; the cup product ∪^n : ∧^nR^1µ_∗Ô → R^nµ_∗Ô is an isomorphism, so Sch^n_X := ∪^n ∘ ∧^nSch^1 : Ω^n_X(−n) ≅ R^nµ_∗Ô_X and R^nµ_∗Ô_X is coherent [Sch13b, Proposition 3.23].
items.note: Cited from Scholze's rigid p-adic Hodge theory and survey; BMS18's extraction routes the same paper's finiteness theorem to P8.

items.name: Lemma 3.4.5 (Künneth for Sch′^1 on tori)
items.statement: On a torus T^d, Sch′^1 is compatible with the Künneth decomposition along the projections.
items.note: Via [Sch13a, Corollaries 6.14, 6.19, Definition 6.8] and the B^+_dR de Rham complex.

items.name: Notation 3.4.6 (the toric perfectoid cover and almost purity)
items.statement: For R^+ = O_C⟨T_1^{±1}, …, T_d^{±1}⟩ and an étale X → T^d, the pro-étale Γ = Z_p(1)^d-torsor X_∞ → X adjoining p-power roots of the T_i is affinoid perfectoid [Sch13a, Lemma 4.5]; H^i_cont(Γ, S_∞) ≅ Γ(X, R^iλ_∗Ô) almost, and H^i_cont(Γ, Z_p) ⊗ S ≅ H^i_cont(Γ, S_∞) [Sch13a, Lemma 5.5].
items.note: AI.3 plans the toric perfectoid cover of a small framed affine, its continuous cochains and the almost purity comparison.

items.name: Lemmas 3.4.7–3.4.8 (Scholze's map on dlog T)
items.statement: In the framed setting Sch′^1_X(dT_i/T_i) = pr_i ∈ H^1_cont(Γ, Z_p(1)) ⊗ R; in dimension one, Sch′^1(dT/T) = id, computed via the Kummer boundary δ and the Čech/Cartan–Leray description.
items.note: Following [Ros23, Proposition F.2.1]. The proof of Lemma 3.4.8 writes α(δ(X)) for α(δ(T)) (sourceIssues E5).

items.name: Corollary 3.4.9 (Scholze's map and finite étale traces)
items.statement: For finite étale f : X′ → X of smooth rigid C-spaces of pure dimension d, Sch^d_X ∘ Tr_f(−d) = H^d(Tr_{an,f}) ∘ f_∗Sch^d_{X′}, with Tr_{an,f} the pro-étale trace of Definition D.7.
items.note: Via [Sch13a, Lemma 5.2], [Zav21a, Corollary D.5], Lemmas 2.7.9, 3.4.7 and D.13.

items.name: Remarks 3.4.10–3.4.11 (generic fibres of R̃^n and dlog)
items.statement: For an admissible 𝔛 with smooth generic fibre, (R̃^nν_∗Ô^+)_C ≅ R^nµ_∗Ô_X, and dlog is an isomorphism on the generic fibre.
items.note: Via Lemmas C.4 and C.9.

items.name: Theorem 3.4.12 (BMS and Scholze agree on the generic fibre)
items.statement: For 𝔛 admissible with reduced special fibre and smooth generic fibre, Sch^n_X ∘ (id ⊗ (dlog^∨)^{⊗n}) = (Φ^n_𝔛)_C, and (Φ^n_𝔛)_C is an isomorphism.
items.note: Reduce to n = 1 and a smooth model finite étale over Ĝ^d_m [Bha18, Lemma 4.9]; [BMS18, Proposition 8.17] (BMS^1(dT/T) = dlog ⊗ 1) and Lemma 3.4.8.

items.name: Theorem/Definition 3.4.13, Definition 3.4.14 (Ψ on the generic fibre)
items.statement: (Ψ′^n_𝔛)_C : (R̃^nν_∗Ô^+)_C ≅ Ω^n_X(−n) and (Ψ^d_𝔛)_C : (R^dν_∗Ô^+)_C → (ω_𝔛)_C(−d) via s_𝔛; by Remark 3.4.15, (Ψ^d_𝔛)_C is (Sch^d_X)^{−1} under these identifications and is independent of the model.

items.name: Definition 3.5.1 (nice admissible formal O_C-schemes)
items.statement: An admissible formal O_C-scheme of dimension d is nice if it is separated with smooth generic fibre of pure dimension d and reduced special fibre.

items.name: Theorem 3.5.2 (the integral Faltings map in degree d)
items.statement: For nice 𝔛 there is a unique O_𝔛-linear Tr^{d,+}_{F,𝔛} : R^dν_∗Ô^+_X → ω_𝔛(−d) restricting to Ψ^d on the smooth locus 𝔛^sm and to (Ψ^d_𝔛)_C on the generic fibre.
items.note: Glued by Theorem 2.5.5.

items.name: Definition 3.5.3 (integral Faltings' trace)
items.statement: Tr^+_{F,𝔛} : Rν_∗Ô^{+,a}_X → ω^a_𝔛(−d)[−d], the composite of the truncation Rν_∗Ô^{+,a} → R^dν_∗Ô^{+,a}[−d] (Rν_∗Ô^{+,a} ∈ D^{[0,d]}_acoh by [Zav21a, Theorem 6.13.6]) with Tr^{d,+}_{F,𝔛}.

items.name: Lemma 3.5.4 (Faltings' trace on the generic fibre)
items.statement: The generic fibre of Tr^{d,+}_{F,𝔛} is (Sch^d_X)^{−1} under the identifications of Remark 3.4.10 and Lemma 2.7.3.

items.name: Definition 3.5.5 (Faltings' trace)
items.statement: Tr_{F,𝔛} : Rν_∗(O^{+,a}_X/p) → ω^{•,a}_{𝔛_0}(−d)[−2d], the reduction of Tr^+_{F,𝔛} mod p via the projection formula and base change ω^•_𝔛 ⊗^L O_{𝔛_0} ≅ ω^•_{𝔛_0}.
items.note: Remark 3.5.6 notes an earlier version for general rig-smooth models; the paper credits the idea to Faltings and Gabber.

items.name: Definition 3.6.1 (pseudo-finite morphisms)
items.statement: A rig-finite morphism f : 𝔛′ → 𝔛 of nice formal schemes of dimension d is pseudo-finite if Rf_∗Rν_∗Ô^{+,a}_{X′} ∈ D^{[0,d]}(𝔛)^a; finite morphisms and rig-isomorphisms are pseudo-finite (Example 3.6.2).

items.name: Construction 3.6.3 and Lemma 3.6.4 (Faltings' trace and finite traces)
items.statement: For a rig-étale pseudo-finite f : 𝔛′ → 𝔛 of nice formal schemes, Tr_𝔣(−d)[−d] ∘ f_∗(Tr^{+,a}_{F,𝔛′}) = Tr^+_{F,𝔛} ∘ Tr^+_{Zar,𝔣}, with Tr^+_{Zar,𝔣} the pro-étale trace of Definition D.8.
items.note: By O_C-flatness of ω_𝔛(−d), checked on the generic fibre via Lemma D.11, Lemma 3.5.4 and Corollary 3.4.9. The proof cites Lemma 2.3.5 where Corollary 2.4.5 is meant (sourceIssues E6).

items.name: Corollary 3.6.5 (compatibility of Faltings' pairings)
items.statement: For f as in Lemma 3.6.4 the diagram (3.9) relating the cup-product pairings on Rf_{0,∗}Rν_∗(O^{+,a}_{X′}/p) and Rν_∗(O^{+,a}_X/p), Tr_{Zar,f}, the restriction Res_f, Tr_{F,𝔛′}, Tr_{F,𝔛} and Tr_{𝔣_0} commutes in D(𝔛)^a.

items.name: Lemma 3.6.6 (Faltings' trace is étale local)
items.statement: For an étale f : 𝔛 → 𝔜 of nice formal schemes, f^∗Tr^+_{F,𝔜} is identified with Tr^+_{F,𝔛} under the isomorphisms Lf^∗Rν_{𝔜,∗}Ô^{+,a} ≅ Rν_{𝔛,∗}Ô^{+,a} ([Zav21a, Theorem 6.13.5]) and f^∗ω_𝔜 ≅ ω_𝔛 (Lemma 2.4.7).

items.name: Almost coherent sheaves on admissible formal schemes (Zavyalov 2021a)
items.statement: Almost coherent O_C-modules and adically quasi-coherent almost coherent O_𝔛-modules, D_acoh(𝔛)^a as the Verdier quotient of D(𝔛) by complexes with almost zero cohomology [Zav21a, Definition 3.4.2, Theorem 3.4.9], the equivalence M ↦ M^∆ on affines [Lemma 4.6.1, 4.5.14] and almost coherence of proper pushforwards [Theorem 5.1.6].
items.note: Imported from the author's memoir [Zav21a] (Mem. EMS 19, 2025); P0 supplies only the abstract almost category.

items.name: Almost internal Hom RalHom
items.statement: RalHom_𝔛(F, G) ∈ D(𝔛)^a for F, G ∈ D(𝔛)^a [Zav21a, Definition 3.5.6], with its adjunctions and the identification RalHom(F^a, G^a)^{hG} ≅ RalHom(F^a_{hG}, G^a) for a finite group G (Lemma 4.4.15; [Zav21a, Propositions 3.5.8, 3.5.14, 3.5.20]).

items.name: Almost Grothendieck duality (Zavyalov 2021a, Theorem 5.5.5)
items.statement: For a proper morphism f_0 : 𝔛_0 → Spec O_C/p of finitely presented O_C/p-schemes, Rf_{0,∗} : D^+_aqc(𝔛_0)^a → D^+_aqc(O_C/p)^a has a right adjoint f_0^!, compatible with f_0^!(O_C/p) = ω^•_{𝔛_0}, and the duality morphism RΓ(𝔛_0, RalHom(F, ω^{•,a})) ≅ RalHom(RΓ(𝔛_0, F), O^a_C/p) holds for almost coherent F [Zav21a, Lemma 5.5.6].

items.name: Almost coherence and amplitude of Rν_∗(O^+/p) (Zavyalov 2021a, Theorems 6.13.5–6.13.6)
items.statement: For an admissible 𝔛 with smooth generic fibre of pure dimension d, Rν_∗(O^{+,a}_X/p) ∈ D^{[0,d]}_acoh(𝔛_0)^a and Rν_∗Ô^{+,a}_X ∈ D^{[0,d]}_acoh(𝔛)^a, compatibly with étale base change and reduction mod p; for proper smooth X of dimension d, RΓ(X, O^+_X/p) is almost concentrated in [0, 2d] [Zav21a, Theorem 6.3.3, Lemma C.6.10].

items.name: Definition 4.1.1 (Faltings' pairing and the duality morphism)
items.statement: For nice 𝔛, Faltings' pairing Rν_∗(O^{+,a}/p) ⊗^L Rν_∗(O^{+,a}/p) →∪ Rν_∗(O^{+,a}/p) →Tr_{F,𝔛} ω^{•,a}_{𝔛_0}(−d)[−2d] (4.1) and the duality morphism D_𝔛 : Rν_∗(O^{+,a}/p) → RalHom(Rν_∗(O^{+,a}/p), ω^{•,a}_{𝔛_0}(−d)[−2d]).

items.name: Definitions 4.2.1–4.2.2 (model polystable and polystable formal schemes)
items.statement: A model polystable formal O_C-scheme is Spf O_C⟨t_{1,0}, …, t_{l,n_l}⟩/(t_{1,0}⋯t_{1,n_1} − ϖ_1, …, t_{l,0}⋯t_{l,n_l} − ϖ_l) with ϖ_i ∈ O_C ∖ {0}; an admissible 𝔛 is polystable if étale locally it admits an étale morphism to a model polystable scheme. With ϖ_i ≠ 0 polystable formal schemes are rig-smooth (Remark 4.2.3).
items.note: Following [Zav21b]; they generalize the semistable models of [ČK19].

items.name: Lemma 4.2.4 (affine polystable algebras)
items.statement: If Spf A is affine polystable, A = A°_K and A is integrally closed in A_K.
items.note: Via Corollary B.8.

items.name: Lemmas 4.2.5 and 4.2.7 (dualizing complexes of polystable schemes)
items.statement: For polystable 𝔛 (generic fibre of pure dimension d), each ω^•_{𝔛_n} and ω^•_𝔛 is a rank-one locally free sheaf placed in degree −d; for a model polystable scheme there are canonical isomorphisms ω^•_{𝔛_n} ≅ O[d] and ω^•_𝔛 ≅ O_𝔛[d].
items.note: Koszul-regularity of the model ([Stacks 063E, 0BR0, 063H]).

items.name: The standard cover of a model polystable scheme (4.2)–(4.5) and Lemma 4.2.8
items.statement: R^+_m adjoins p^m-th roots of the t_{i,j} compatibly with the equations; Spf R^+_m is again model polystable, R^+_m = R°_m is finitely presented over R^+ [Bos14, Theorem 7.3/4], Spf R^+_m → Spf R^+ is finite and rig-étale, Γ_m ≅ ∏_i µ^{n_i}_{p^m} (embedded in ∏_i µ^{n_i+1}_{p^m}) acts and Spa(R_m) → Spa(R) is a finite étale Γ_m-torsor; R^+_∞ := (colim R^+_m)^∧.

items.name: Definition 4.2.9 (integral perfectoid rings)
items.statement: A p-adically complete p-torsion-free ring R with ϖ^p | p for some ϖ is integral perfectoid if Frobenius induces R/ϖ ≅ R/ϖ^p [BMS18, Definition 3.5, Lemma 3.10].
items.note: PerfectoidQuotients Q0 plans integral perfectoid rings.

items.name: Lemma 4.2.11 (the limit of the standard cover is perfectoid)
items.statement: R^+_∞ is integral perfectoid, (R_∞, R^+_∞) is a perfectoid pair, and lim Spa(R_m) → Spa(R) is a pro-étale Γ-torsor with Γ ≅ Z_p(1)^d (Remark 4.2.12).
items.note: Via [BMS18, Lemma 3.20], [Bha, Lemma 5.1.2].

items.name: Lemma 4.2.13 (almost purity for polystable models)
items.statement: RΓ_cont(Γ, R^+_∞)^{L∆} → Rν_∗Ô^+_X is an almost isomorphism, and likewise mod p.
items.note: Cartan–Leray with almost purity ([Sch13a, Lemmas 4.12, 5.6]) and [Zav21a, §4.8, Definition 4.8.7, Corollary 4.8.14].

items.name: Weight decomposition of R^+ and R^+_∞ (Remark 4.2.14–Remark 4.2.20)
items.statement: With T ⊂ G_m^{d+l} the torus of the equations and Γ ≅ Hom(X(T)[1/p]/X(T), µ_{p^∞}) = T_p(T), R^+ = ⊕̂_{χ∈X(T)} V_χ (4.6) with V_χ ⊗ V_χ′ ≅ V_{χ+χ′}, R^+_m = ⊕̂_{χ∈p^{−m}X(T)} V_χ (Lemma 4.2.15); for χ ∈ X(T)[1/p], R^+_χ := ⊕̂_{χ′∈χ+X(T)} V_χ′ (Definition 4.2.17), R^+_m = ⊕ R^+_χ̄ (Lemma 4.2.19) and R^+_∞ = ⊕̂ R^+_χ̄ with Γ acting on R^+_χ̄ through χ (Remark 4.2.20).

items.name: Lemma 4.2.21 and Warning 4.2.22 (the modules R^+_χ)
items.statement: If l = 1 and ϖ is a unit, each R^+_χ is free of rank one; in general R^+_χ need not be flat.
items.note: Proof left to the reader.

items.name: Continuous cohomology of Z_p^d as a Koszul complex (Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze, Lemma 7.3)
items.statement: For Γ ≅ Z_p^d with basis γ_1, …, γ_d and a p-adically complete module M with continuous action, RΓ_cont(Γ, M) ≅ K(M; γ_1 − 1, …, γ_d − 1).
items.locator: §4.2.3, proof of Lemma 4.2.23, p. 55; proof of Lemma 4.3.10, p. 62
items.note: AI.3 plans the continuous group cochains of the toric cover via the canonical cohomology carrier; ArithmeticGaloisDuality D7 plans continuous cohomology.

items.name: Lemma 4.2.23 (cohomology of Γ with coefficients in R^+_χ)
items.statement: For χ = Σ a_i/p^{m_i} e_i with m = m_k = max m_i: (1) H^i_cont(Γ, R^+_χ) = 0 for i > d; (2) it is finitely presented over R^+; (3) it is killed by ζ_{p^{m_k}} − 1; (4) it is M_i ⊗_{O_C} R^+_χ for a finitely presented O_C-module M_i, and has no nonzero 𝔪-torsion.
items.note: Koszul complex K(O_C; ζ^{a_1}_{p^{m_1}} − 1, …) ⊗ R^+_χ ([BMS18, Lemma 7.3, Definition 7.1], [Stacks 0663], [Sch13a, Propositions 2.8, 2.10]). The proof mixes the indices i and j (sourceIssues E7).

items.name: Corollaries 4.2.25–4.2.26 (cohomology of Γ with coefficients in R^+_∞)
items.statement: Mod p, H^i_cont(Γ, R^+_χ/p) vanishes for i > d, is finitely presented and is killed by p^{1/n} for all but finitely many χ̄. For R^+_∞: (1) H^i = 0 for i > d; (2) H^i_cont(Γ, R^+) ≅ ∧^i(R^+)^d; (3) H^i_cont(Γ, R^+_∞) = H^i_cont(Γ, R^+) ⊕ N_i with N_i killed by 1 − ζ_p ([ČK19, Lemma 3.6]); (4) no nonzero 𝔪-torsion; (5) almost finitely presented ([Zav21a, Theorem 2.13.2]).

items.name: Lemma 4.2.27 and Corollary 4.2.28 (Lη_{1−ζ_p} makes the comparison integral)
items.statement: For model polystable Spf R^+, Lη_{1−ζ_p}RΓ_cont(Γ, R^+_∞) → Lη_{1−ζ_p}RΓ(X, Ô^+_X) is an isomorphism; the sheaf version Lη_{1−ζ_p}(RΓ_cont(Γ, R^+_∞)^{L∆}) ≅ Lη_{1−ζ_p}Rν_∗Ô^+_X holds on 𝔛.
items.note: [BMS18, Corollary 6.5, Lemma 8.11(ii)] with Corollary 4.2.26(4); [Zav21a, Lemma 4.8.13, Theorem 4.8.15], [BMS18, Lemma 6.4].

items.name: Corollary 4.2.29 (polystable: R^iν_∗Ô^+ modulo torsion)
items.statement: For polystable 𝔛 with generic fibre of pure dimension d, R^iν_∗Ô^+/(R^iν_∗Ô^+)[1 − ζ_p] is locally free of rank C(d, i) and equals R̃^iν_∗Ô^+.

items.name: Theorem 4.2.30 (Faltings' map is an isomorphism for polystable models)
items.statement: For 𝔛 separated polystable with X of pure dimension d, Tr^{+,d}_{F,𝔛} induces an honest isomorphism t^+_𝔛 : R^dν_∗Ô^+/(R^dν_∗Ô^+)[1 − ζ_p] ≅ ω_𝔛(−d) ≅ ω^•_𝔛(−d)[−d].
items.note: Both sides are rank-one locally free (Lemma 4.2.7, Corollary 4.2.29); by Lemma 2.5.4 check on 𝔛^sm ([BMS18, Theorem 8.3]) and the generic fibre ([Sch13b, Proposition 3.23]). Generalizes [BMS18, Theorem 8.3] to polystable models.

items.name: Definition 4.3.1 and Theorem 4.3.2 (duality for A_m/A in characteristic p)
items.statement: For A = F_p[t_0, …, t_n]/(t_0⋯t_n) and A_m = A[t_i^{1/p^m}], tr_m : A_m → A keeps the monomials with integral exponents; the pairing A_m ⊗^L_A A_m → A_m →tr_m A is perfect, i.e. α_m : A_m ≅ RHom_A(A_m, A).
items.note: Via dualizing complexes of the normal-crossing schemes and [Stacks 0AX2].

items.name: Definition 4.3.3 (the trace tr^+_m)
items.statement: tr^+_m : R^+_m → R^+ is the projection onto the trivial-character summand.

items.name: Lemmas 4.3.4–4.3.5 (RHom over topologically finitely presented algebras)
items.statement: For A topologically finitely presented over O_C and M ∈ D^−_acoh(A), RHom_A(M, A) ∈ D^+_acoh(A) and is derived p-complete; RHom is compatible with completed tensor products (a Künneth formula, by derived Nakayama).
items.note: Via [Zav21a, Proposition 2.6.19, 2.4.8(i)], [Stacks 0A6E, 091T, 0G1U, 0A6A]; footnote 20 writes R, S for A, B.

items.name: Proposition 4.3.6 and Corollary 4.3.7 (duality for the standard cover)
items.statement: R^+_m ⊗^L_{R^+} R^+_m → R^+_m →tr^+_m R^+ is perfect, i.e. R^+_m ≅ RHom_{R^+}(R^+_m, R^+); for each χ, R^+_χ ⊗^L R^+_{−χ} → R^+ is perfect; likewise mod p (Remark 4.3.8).
items.note: Reduce to l = 1 (Lemma 4.3.5); if ϖ is a unit use Lemma 4.2.21; otherwise reduce mod π with |ϖ^{1/p^n}| < |π| < 1 to Theorem 4.3.2.

items.name: Definitions 4.3.9 and 4.3.13 (group-cohomology traces)
items.statement: tr_Γ : RΓ_cont(Γ, R^+) → H^d_cont(Γ, R^+)[−d] = R^+[−d] (Corollary 4.2.26(2)) and its mod p version; tr_{Γ,∞} : RΓ_cont(Γ, R^+_∞) → R^+[−d] through the trivial character, equivalently through H^d/[1 − ζ_p] (Remark 4.3.14).

items.name: Lemma 4.3.10 (Poincaré duality for continuous cohomology of Z_p^d)
items.statement: If M, N are R^+/p-modules with continuous R^+/p-linear Γ-actions and M ⊗^L N → R^+/p is a Γ-invariant perfect pairing, then RΓ_cont(Γ, M) ⊗^L RΓ_cont(Γ, N) → RΓ_cont(Γ, R^+/p) →tr_Γ/p R^+/p[−d] is perfect.
items.note: Via [BMS18, Lemma 7.3], RΓ(Z^d, −) and topological Poincaré duality for B(Z^d) = (S^1)^d; footnote 24: the two traces agree up to a unit.

items.name: Lemmas 4.3.11–4.3.12 (duality for R^+_χ and completeness)
items.statement: RΓ_cont(Γ, R^+_χ) and RΓ_cont(Γ, R^+_{−χ}) are dual under tr_Γ; RΓ_cont(Γ, R^+_∞) and its R^+-dual are derived p-complete.
items.note: Via [Stacks 091T, 091U], [Zav21a, Lemma 2.12.7, Proposition 2.6.19].

items.name: Theorem 4.3.15 (almost duality for RΓ_cont(Γ, R^+_∞))
items.statement: RΓ_cont(Γ, R^+_∞) ⊗^L_{R^+} RΓ_cont(Γ, R^+_∞) → RΓ_cont(Γ, R^+_∞) →tr_{Γ,∞} R^+[−d] is almost perfect.
items.note: Sum over characters with Corollary 4.2.25(3) and [Zav21a, Lemma A.4].

items.name: Theorem 4.3.16 (local almost duality for polystable models)
items.statement: For 𝔛 separated polystable with X of pure dimension d, Rν_∗Ô^{+,a}_X ⊗^L Rν_∗Ô^{+,a}_X →∪ Rν_∗Ô^{+,a}_X →Tr_{F,𝔛} ω^a_𝔛(−d)[−d] is almost perfect.
items.note: Étale descent (Lemma 3.6.6, [Zav21a, Theorem 6.13.6, Lemmas 4.9.7, 2.9.12]) to a model; Theorem 4.2.30, Lemma 4.2.13 and Theorem 4.3.15. Step 2 prints ω^a_{𝔛_0} for ω^a_𝔛 (sourceIssues E8).

items.name: Corollary 4.3.17 (mod p local duality for polystable models)
items.statement: For such 𝔛, Faltings' pairing (4.1) on Rν_∗(O^{+,a}_X/p) is almost perfect.
items.note: Reduce Theorem 4.3.16 mod p using ω^•_𝔛 ≅ ω_𝔛[d].

items.name: Theorem 4.4.1 (local altered uniformization, Zavyalov 2021b)
items.statement: For an admissible 𝔛 with smooth generic fibre there are finitely many (𝔛_i, f_i) obtained from 𝔛 by open Zariski covers and rig-isomorphisms such that each 𝔛_i is a geometric quotient 𝔛′_i/G_i by a finite group with 𝔛′_{i,C} → 𝔛_{i,C} a G_i-torsor, and each 𝔛′_i admits a rig-isomorphism from a polystable rig-smooth 𝔛″_i; all intermediate schemes can be taken with reduced quasi-projective special fibres.
items.note: Cited from [Zav21b, Theorem 1.4] (Israel J. Math. 263, 2024), building on Temkin's altered local uniformization; quotients exist by [Zav21c, Remark 3.3.3, Theorem 3.3.4] and (R^{ic})^G = (R^G)^{ic} for the normalization of Definition B.10.

items.name: Definition 4.4.2 (good quotients)
items.statement: A morphism 𝔛′ → 𝔛 of nice formal schemes is a good quotient by a finite group G if 𝔛 = 𝔛′/G is a geometric quotient, the special fibres are quasi-projective and 𝔛′_C → 𝔛_C is a G-torsor.
items.note: Quotients of admissible formal schemes by finite groups are constructed in [Zav21c].

items.name: Lemma 4.4.3 (descent along rig-isomorphisms)
items.statement: If π : 𝔛′ → 𝔛 is a rig-isomorphism of nice formal schemes and Faltings' pairing is almost perfect on 𝔛′, it is almost perfect on 𝔛.
items.note: Corollary 3.6.5 and almost Grothendieck duality for π_0 ([Zav21a, Lemma 5.5.6]).

items.name: Definitions 4.4.4 and 4.4.10 (equivariant modules and homotopy (co)invariants)
items.statement: G-equivariant O_X-modules Mod^G_X for a finite group G acting trivially on X (a Grothendieck abelian category, Remarks 4.4.5–4.4.9: K-injectives, Rf_∗ on D^G); homotopy invariants F^{hG} = RHom_{O[G]}(O, F) and coinvariants F_{hG} = F ⊗^L_{O[G]} O.

items.name: Lemma 4.4.11 (Rt_∗ commutes with homotopy (co)invariants)
items.statement: Rt_∗ : D(O^+/p[G]) → D(O_{𝔛_0}[G]) commutes with homotopy invariants and coinvariants.
items.note: Via bar resolutions, [Stacks 0A5K], [Hub96, Corollary 2.8.3].

items.name: Definitions 4.4.12, 4.4.14 (almost equivariant modules and almost homotopy (co)invariants)
items.statement: Almost G-equivariant modules Mod^a_{O_X[G]} ([Zav21a, Definition 3.1.9]; O_C central suffices, Remark 4.4.13) and the almost versions of (−)^{hG}, (−)_{hG}.

items.name: Constructions 4.4.16–4.4.18 (G-structures on the pushforward, the trace and the restriction)
items.statement: For a good quotient f : 𝔛′ → 𝔛 by G, G-equivariant structures on Rf_{0,∗}Rν_{X′,∗}(O^{+,a}/p), on Tr_{Zar,f} (Definition D.9) and on Res_f.
items.note: Construction 4.4.17 writes O^+_{𝔛′}/p^n for O^+/p (sourceIssues E9).

items.name: Lemma 4.4.19 (Galois descent for a good quotient)
items.statement: For a good quotient f, Tr_{Zar,f} induces (Rf_{0,∗}Rν_{X′,∗}(O^+/p))_{hG} ≅ Rν_{X,∗}(O^+/p), and Res_f induces Rν_{X,∗}(O^+/p) ≅ (Rf_{0,∗}Rν_{X′,∗}(O^+/p))^{hG}; the almost versions hold too (Remark 4.4.20).
items.note: Via [Sch13a, Corollary 3.17(i)] and [Zav21a, Propositions 3.5.8, 3.5.14, 3.5.23].

items.name: Lemmas 4.4.21–4.4.22 (equivariance of the pairings)
items.statement: For a good quotient f, the diagram of cup products, Tr_{Zar,f} and Res_f commutes in D(O_{𝔛_0}[G])^a; Tr_{f_0} ∘ Rf_{0,∗}Tr_{F,𝔛′} is uniquely G-equivariant and diagram (4.13) commutes in D(O_{𝔛_0}[G])^a.

items.name: Lemma 4.4.23 (descent along good quotients)
items.statement: If f : 𝔛′ → 𝔛 is a good quotient of nice formal schemes and Faltings' pairing is almost perfect on 𝔛′, it is almost perfect on 𝔛.
items.note: Via Lemma 4.4.15 and Lemma 4.4.19.

items.name: Theorem 4.4.24 = Theorem 4.1.2 (local almost duality)
items.statement: Let 𝔛 be a nice admissible formal O_C-scheme: separated, with smooth generic fibre X of pure dimension d and reduced special fibre. Then Faltings' pairing is almost perfect: D_𝔛 : Rν_∗(O^{+,a}_X/p) → RalHom(Rν_∗(O^{+,a}_X/p), ω^{•,a}_{𝔛_0}(−d)[−2d]) is an isomorphism in D(𝔛_0)^a.
items.note: Polystable case (Corollary 4.3.17), then rig-isomorphisms (Lemma 4.4.3), good quotients (Lemma 4.4.23) and Zariski covers via Theorem 4.4.1. Step 3 prints 𝔛′_i → 𝔛′ for 𝔛′_i → 𝔛_i (sourceIssues E11). The statement omits the reduced special fibre ('nice') that Theorem 4.1.2 and Definition 4.1.1 require (sourceIssues E10).

items.name: Scholze's primitive comparison theorem and finiteness
items.statement: For X proper smooth over C, H^i_ét(X, F_p) ⊗_{F_p} O_C/p → H^i(X, O^+_X/p) is an almost isomorphism for all i [Sch13a, Theorem 5.1], and H^i_ét(X, F_p) is finite, vanishing for i > 2 dim X; for proper (not necessarily smooth) X, RΓ_ét(X, F_p) ∈ D^{[0,2d]}_coh(F_p) [Sch13b, Theorem 3.17].
items.note: Cited; BMS18's extraction routes Scholze's finiteness theorem to P8 as its owner, with Scholze (2013) listed as a prerequisite.

items.name: Pro-étale versus étale cohomology of F_p and O^+/p (Scholze, Corollary 3.17)
items.statement: For a rigid C-space, the pro-étale and étale cohomology of F_p(i) and of O^+/p(i) agree, and for finite étale f, f_{proét,∗}(O^+_{X′}/p^n) ≅ λ^{−1}_X(f_{ét,∗}O^+_{X′}/p^n) [Sch13a, Corollary 3.17]; X_proét is a coherent topos for qcqs X [Sch13a, Proposition 3.12(vii)], so RΓ(X_C, Q_p) = RΓ(X_C, Z_p)[1/p].
items.note: Cited from Scholze's rigid p-adic Hodge theory.

items.name: Definitions 5.2.1, 5.2.3 and Lemma 5.2.2 (the global trace)
items.statement: For X smooth proper over C of pure dimension d, choose a nice model 𝔣 : 𝔛 → Spf O_C (it exists by Theorem 2.7.1 and is proper by Lemma B.1) and set Tr^𝔛_X := Tr_{𝔣_0}(−d)[−2d] ∘ RΓ(𝔛_0, Tr_{F,𝔛}) : RΓ(X, O^{+,a}/p) ≅ RΓ(𝔛_0, Rν_∗(O^{+,a}/p)) → O^a_C/p(−d)[−2d]; it is independent of 𝔛 (Lemma 5.2.2, via a dominating model and Corollary 3.6.5), giving Tr_X.
items.note: Definition 5.2.1 prints the target as O^a_C/p(−d)[2d] (sourceIssues E12).

items.name: Theorem 5.1.1 = Theorem 5.2.4 (global almost duality for O^+/p)
items.statement: For X smooth proper over C of pure dimension d, RΓ(X, O^{+,a}_X/p) ⊗^L_{O_C/p} RΓ(X, O^{+,a}_X/p) →∪ RΓ(X, O^{+,a}_X/p) →Tr_X O^a_C/p(−d)[−2d] is almost perfect.
items.note: From Theorem 4.4.24 and almost Grothendieck duality for 𝔛_0 ([Zav21a, Lemma 5.5.6]), with [Stacks 0FP6] for cup products.

items.name: Theorem 5.2.5 (almost duality in each degree)
items.statement: For X smooth proper over C of pure dimension d, H^i(X, O^{+,a}_X/p) ⊗ H^{2d−i}(X, O^{+,a}_X/p) → H^{2d}(X, O^{+,a}_X/p) →Tr_X O^a_C/p(−d) is almost perfect for every i ≥ 0.
items.note: The H^i are almost projective by the primitive comparison and [Zav21a, Lemma 2.2.6].

items.name: Definition 5.3.1 (dimension of locally spectral spaces and morphisms)
items.statement: Krull dimension of a locally spectral space, pure dimension, and the dimension of a morphism of rigid spaces as in [Hub96, Definition 1.8.1].

items.name: Lemma 5.3.2 (cohomological dimension of Rf_!)
items.statement: For a partially proper morphism f : X → Y of rigid K-spaces of pure dimension d and F ∈ Shv(X_ét, Λ), Λ = Z/n, R^if_!F = 0 for i > 2d.
items.note: [Hub96, Proposition 5.3.11, Corollary 1.8.7]; H3 plans the finite cohomological-dimension statements for curves.

items.name: Theorem 5.3.3 (Berkovich's trace for smooth partially proper morphisms)
items.statement: For f : X → Y a partially proper smooth morphism of rigid K-spaces of pure dimension d and Λ = Z/n (n arbitrary), there is t_f : R^{2d}f_!Λ(d) → Λ that (1) is compatible with geometric fibres over maximal points, (2) satisfies t_g □ t_f = t_{g∘f}, (3) is the adjunction map for d = 0, and (4) is surjective if all fibres are nonempty.
items.note: Translated from [Ber93, Theorem 7.2.1] through the Huber–Berkovich comparison of Appendix A (Lemma A.8, Theorem A.15, Lemma A.19) and overconvergence [Hub96, Corollary 8.2.4]; GUO-REINECKE-24 routed this trace to H3.

items.name: Theorem 5.4.2 (the trace is an isomorphism)
items.statement: For X smooth proper geometrically connected over K of pure dimension d, t_X : H^{2d}_ét(X_C, F_p(d)) → F_p is an isomorphism of Galois representations.
items.note: t_X is the Berkovich trace for X_C (Remark 5.4.1). Surjective by Theorem 5.3.3(4); dimension one from primitive comparison, [Sch13a, Proposition 2.10] and Theorem 5.2.4.

items.name: Lemma 5.4.3 (detecting isomorphisms after ⊗ O_C/p)
items.statement: A map f : V → W of finite-dimensional F_p-vector spaces is an isomorphism if and only if f ⊗ O_C/p is an almost isomorphism.

items.name: Theorem 5.4.4 = Theorem 1.1.4 = Theorem 5.1.2 (mod p Poincaré duality)
items.statement: Let X be a smooth proper rigid-analytic space of pure dimension d over a non-archimedean field K of mixed characteristic (0, p). The Galois-equivariant trace t_X : H^{2d}_ét(X_K̂̄, F_p(d)) → F_p makes H^i_ét(X_K̂̄, F_p) ⊗ H^{2d−i}_ét(X_K̂̄, F_p(d)) →∪ H^{2d}_ét(X_K̂̄, F_p(d)) →t_X F_p a perfect pairing of continuous Galois representations for every i ≥ 0.
items.note: From Theorem 5.2.5 by the primitive comparison, Lemma 5.4.3 and the compatibility of Tr_X with t_X on each component ([Zav21a, Proposition 2.2.1]). Answers Scholze's question in [Sch13a]; announced by Gabber in 2015.

items.name: Theorem 5.4.5 (Poincaré duality for F_p-local systems)
items.statement: For X smooth proper over K of pure dimension d and an étale F_p-local system L, H^i_ét(X_C, L) ⊗ H^{2d−i}_ét(X_C, L^∨(d)) → H^{2d}_ét(X_C, F_p(d)) →t_X F_p is a perfect Galois-equivariant pairing.
items.note: Méthode de la trace ([Stacks 03SH]): a finite étale cover of degree prime to p on which L is unipotent, with Theorem 5.3.3(2).

items.name: Lemma 5.5.1 (perfectness of p-adic cohomology of proper rigid spaces)
items.statement: For X proper over C of pure dimension d, RΓ_ét(X, Z/p^n) ∈ D^{[0,2d]}_perf(Z/p^n), RΓ(X, Z_p) ∈ D^{[0,2d]}_perf(Z_p), and H^i(X, Z_p) ≅ lim_n H^i_ét(X, Z/p^n).
items.note: [Sch13b, Theorem 3.17] or [Zav21a, Theorem 1.1.2], [Stacks 07LU, 0A07, 09AV], [Zav21a, Lemma A.3] and Mittag-Leffler for the Milnor sequence.

items.name: Theorem 5.5.2 (Z/p^n Poincaré duality)
items.statement: For X smooth proper over K of pure dimension d, RΓ_ét(X_C, Z/p^n) ⊗^L RΓ_ét(X_C, Z/p^n(d)) →∪ RΓ_ét(X_C, Z/p^n(d)) →t_{X,Z/p^n} Z/p^n is a perfect Galois-equivariant pairing for every n ≥ 1.
items.note: Reduce mod p by derived Nakayama for perfect complexes ([Stacks 0A6A]) to Theorem 5.4.4.

items.name: Definition 5.5.3 and Theorem 5.5.4 (Z_p Poincaré duality)
items.statement: t_{X,Z_p} := lim_n t_{X,Z/p^n}, and RΓ(X_C, Z_p) ⊗^L RΓ(X_C, Z_p(d)) → RΓ(X_C, Z_p(d)) →t_{X,Z_p} Z_p is a perfect Galois-equivariant pairing.

items.name: Definition 5.5.5 and Theorem 5.5.6 (Q_p Poincaré duality)
items.statement: t_{X,Q_p} := t_{X,Z_p}[1/p], and RΓ(X_C, Q_p) ⊗^L RΓ(X_C, Q_p(d)) → Q_p is perfect and Galois-equivariant; in particular H^i(X_C, Q_p) ⊗ H^{2d−i}(X_C, Q_p(d)) → Q_p is perfect for every i.

items.name: Definitions A.1 and A.3 (partially proper and taut)
items.statement: A morphism of analytic adic spaces is partially proper if it is locally of +-weakly finite type and every Spa(k, k°) → X over Spa(k, k^+) → Y, for a complete microbial valuation ring k^+, lifts uniquely to Spa(k, k^+) → X (Definition A.1); X is taut if it is quasi-separated and the closure of every quasi-compact subset is quasi-compact, and f is taut if preimages of taut opens are taut [Hub96, Definition 5.1.2]; qcqs and partially proper morphisms are taut [Hub96, Lemmas 5.1.3–5.1.4].
items.locator: Appendix A, Definitions A.1, A.3, Remarks A.2, A.4, p. 84
items.note: H3 plans Huber's proper-support direct image from his partial-properness and support definitions.

items.name: Definitions A.5–A.6 (the categories (A), (A)′ and (An))
items.statement: (A): adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(K, O_K); (A)′: the taut ones; X_max is the set of rank-one points with the quotient topology from ω_X : X → X_max, x ↦ x_gen; (An): Hausdorff strictly K-analytic Berkovich spaces [Ber93, §1.2].
items.note: TB.0 plans Berkovich spectra and gluing affinoids into analytic spaces.

items.name: Huber's comparison of adic and Berkovich spaces (Lemma A.7)
items.statement: Huber's functor s′ : (An) → (A)′ of [Hub96, §8.3] is an equivalence ([Hub96, Proposition 8.3.1, Remark 8.3.2, Lemma 5.6.8(i)], [Hub94, Proposition 4.5(iv)]) with quasi-inverse u; u sends an affinoid open Spa(A, A°) ⊂ X to the affinoid domain M(A) ⊂ u(X), and |u(X)| is functorially X_max (Lemma A.7, [Hub96, Remark 8.3.2], [Hen16, Construction 7.1]).
items.note: TB.0 plans the affinoid point-set comparison of Berkovich and Huber spectra; the global equivalence of categories is the added statement.

items.name: Lemma A.8 and Corollary A.11 (properties under u)
items.statement: For f in (A)′: if f is partially proper (resp. proper, étale, smooth) then u(f) is boundaryless (resp. proper, quasi-étale, quasi-smooth); f is partially proper and étale if and only if u(f) is étale; and u(f) is smooth if f is partially proper and smooth.
items.locator: Appendix A, Lemma A.8, Remarks A.9–A.10, Corollary A.11, Remark A.12, pp. 85–86
items.note: [Duc18, 1.3.20, 5.2.4, 5.2.6, Corollary 5.4.8], [Tem00, Theorem 4.1, Remark 2.6, Corollary 4.4], [Hub96, Corollary 1.3.9, Lemma 2.2.8, Corollary 1.6.10], [Ber93, §3.4], [Ber99, Remark 9.7].

items.name: Definition A.13 (the strict étale site) and the morphism θ_X
items.statement: The strict étale site X_{ét.s} of a strictly K-analytic space (étale X-objects of (An), jointly surjective coverings), whose topos is that of Berkovich's étale site (Remark A.14, [Hub96, p. 426]), and the morphism θ_X : X_ét → u(X)_{ét.s} (A.1) for X in (A)′.
items.locator: Appendix A, Definition A.13, Remark A.14, p. 86

items.name: Theorem A.15 (Huber: compactly supported pushforward and θ)
items.statement: For a partially proper f : X → Y in (A)′ there is a natural isomorphism Rf_!θ^∗_XF ≅ θ^∗_Y Ru(f)_!F for F ∈ D^+(u(X)_{ét.s}, Z), with Huber's Rf_! [Hub96, §5.3] and Berkovich's Ru(f)_! [Ber93, §5.1] ([Hub96, Proposition 8.3.6]).
items.locator: Appendix A, Theorem A.15, Remark A.16, p. 87

items.name: Definition A.17 and Lemma A.18 (overconvergent sheaves)
items.statement: An étale abelian sheaf on X is overconvergent if F_{η_2} → F_{η_1} is an isomorphism for every specialization η_1 ⇝ η_2 of geometric points [Hub96, Definition 8.2.1]; for taut X, θ^∗_X is an equivalence Ab(u(X)_{ét.s}) ≅ Ab^ov(X_ét) [Hub96, Theorem 8.3.5].
items.locator: Appendix A, Definition A.17, Lemma A.18, p. 87

items.name: Lemma A.19 (traces for partially proper étale maps)
items.statement: For a partially proper étale f : X → Y of taut rigid spaces, the trace t_f : f_!f^∗ → id (f_! ⊣ f^∗ by [Hub96, Lemma 2.7.6]) and Berkovich's trace t^B_{u(f)} ([Ber93, Remark 5.4.2(ii)]) correspond under θ^∗_Y and α_f.
items.note: Formal from Lemma A.18, Theorem A.15 and [Hub96, Proposition 8.2.3, Corollary 8.2.4].

items.name: Lemma B.1 (Lütkebohmert–Temkin: separatedness and properness via models)
items.statement: For a morphism f of admissible formal O_K-schemes, f is separated (resp. proper) if and only if f_K is so in Huber's sense if and only if f_K is so in Kiehl's sense.
items.note: F0 plans the properness, separatedness and smoothness comparisons with formal models ([Hub96, Remark 1.3.18], [Hub93, 3.11.20, 3.12.5], [Tem00, Corollary 4.5], [Lüt90]).

items.name: Lemmas B.2–B.3 and Corollary B.4 (dimension of models)
items.statement: X is of pure dimension d iff every affinoid Spa(A, A°) ⊂ X has dim A = d [Hub96, Lemma 1.8.6]; for flat topologically finite type A over O_K, dim A_K = dim A_k; hence an admissible model of a rigid space of pure dimension d has special fibre of pure dimension d.
items.locator: Appendix B, Lemmas B.2–B.3, Corollary B.4, pp. 88–89
items.note: Noether normalization [FK18, 9.2.10], [Bos14, 2.2/17], [Mat80, Theorem 20].

items.name: Lemma B.5 (Elkik's algebraization with pure relative dimension)
items.statement: If Spf B is an affine admissible formal O_K-scheme with smooth generic fibre of pure dimension d, there is a flat finitely presented O_K-algebra A with Â ≅ B, A_K smooth and A of pure relative dimension d.
items.note: [Tem17, Theorem 3.1.3] (after [Elk73, Théorème 7, Remarque 2(c)] and [Tem08, Proposition 3.3.2]); discard the components inside the generic fibre and use [Gro66, Lemme 14.3.10].

items.name: Lemmas B.6–B.7 and Corollary B.8 (reduced special fibres)
items.statement: For flat topologically finite type A over O_K: every nonzero f ∈ A_K has a scalar multiple cf ∈ A with nonzero reduction; if A_k is reduced then A is reduced and A = A°_K ([Lüt16, Proposition 3.4.1]), so A is integrally closed in A_K; conversely for K algebraically closed, A integrally closed in A_K implies A_k reduced.
items.locator: Appendix B, Lemmas B.6–B.7, Corollary B.8, pp. 89–90
items.note: [Bos14, Proposition 3.1/5, Theorem 3.1/17(ii)].

items.name: Theorem B.9 (the Reduced Fibre Theorem, finite rig-isomorphism form)
items.statement: For K algebraically closed and 𝔛 admissible with reduced generic fibre there is a unique finite rig-isomorphism π : 𝔛̃ → 𝔛 with reduced special fibre, universal among maps from admissible formal schemes with reduced special fibre; on affines 𝔛̃ = Spf A°_K. It is the normalization of 𝔛 in X_K (Definition B.10), functorial in 𝔛 (Remark B.11).
items.locator: Appendix B, Theorem B.9, Definition B.10, Remark B.11, pp. 90–91
items.note: Existence is the easy case of [BLR95, Theorem 2.1] via [BLR95, Theorem 1.3] and [Bos14, Theorem 3.1/17].

items.name: Lemma B.12 (connected components)
items.statement: If 𝔛 has reduced special fibre, every connected component of X_K is the generic fibre of a connected component of 𝔛.
items.note: Idempotents via Corollary B.8.

items.name: Lemma B.13 and Corollaries B.14–B.15 (good dense opens)
items.statement: For a rig-finite f : 𝔛 → 𝔜 with 𝔜 of geometrically reduced special fibre there is a dense open 𝔘 ⊂ 𝔜^sm over which f is finite and flat; if 𝔛 also has geometrically reduced special fibre, 𝔘 can be chosen with 𝔛_𝔘 O_K-smooth; if f is a rig-isomorphism, f is an isomorphism over some dense open 𝔘 ⊂ 𝔜^sm.
items.locator: Appendix B, Lemma B.13, Corollaries B.14–B.15, pp. 91–92

items.name: Definition C.1 and Lemma C.4–Corollary C.5 (generic fibre of complexes)
items.statement: For 𝔛 admissible over a perfectoid O_K, F_K := Lsp^∗_𝔛F for sp_𝔛 : (X_an, O_X) → (𝔛_Zar, O_𝔛), which is flat [FK18, Corollary II.5.1.4]; F_K = 0 for ϖ^∞-torsion F (Definition C.3), so (−)_K factors through D(𝔛)^a.
items.locator: Appendix C, Definitions C.1, C.3, Remark C.2, Lemma C.4, Corollary C.5, p. 92

items.name: Lemmas C.6–C.7 (coherence of generic fibres)
items.statement: (−)_K sends D_acoh(𝔛)^a to D_coh(X), with (M^∆)_K ≅ (M[1/ϖ])^~ on affines; for F ∈ D^+_coh(X), F → (Rsp_{𝔛,∗}F)_K is an isomorphism.
items.note: Via [Zav21a, Lemmas 4.6.1, 4.5.14] and [FK18, Proposition 6.5.1].

items.name: Lemma C.8 (proper base change for generic fibres)
items.statement: For proper π : 𝔛′ → 𝔛, the base change map (Rπ_∗F)_K → Rπ_{K,∗}(F_K) is an isomorphism for F ∈ D^+_acoh(𝔛′)^a or D^+_acoh(𝔛′).
items.note: Via [Zav21a, Theorem 5.1.6], Lemma B.1, [FK18, Theorem 7.5.19, Theorem I.7.1.1] and Čech complexes.

items.name: Lemma C.9 (generic fibre of Rν_∗Ô^+)
items.statement: For smooth X with admissible model 𝔛, (Rν_∗Ô^+_X)_K ≅ (Rν_∗Ô_X)_K ≅ Rµ_∗Ô_X.
items.note: Via Lemma C.4, Lemma C.7 and coherence of Rµ_∗Ô_X [Sch13b, Proposition 3.23].

items.name: Definition D.1 (étale trace of a finite étale morphism)
items.statement: For finite étale f : X′ → X, f_∗ = f_! on étale abelian sheaves [Hub96, Definition 5.2.1, Proposition 5.2.4], and Tr_{ét,f,F} : f_∗f^{−1}F → F is the counit of (f_∗, f^{−1}); in particular Tr_{ét,f} : f_∗O^+_{X′} → O^+_X and f_∗(O^+_{X′}/p) → O^+_X/p.
items.locator: Appendix D, Definition D.1, Remark D.2, p. 95
items.note: H3 plans the compatibility of traces with finite étale maps and H0 the classical étale direct image. The second displayed trace is labelled O^+_X/p^n (sourceIssues E9).

items.name: Definitions D.3, D.5–D.7 and Lemma D.4 (pro-étale traces)

routes.title: The classical analytic cohomology inputs to diamonds, Part II: mod-p Poincaré duality for smooth proper rigid spaces
routes.brief:
Starts where The classical analytic cohomology inputs to diamonds (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology) stops: H3 plans Huber's trace and Poincaré duality for smooth curves with torsion prime to p. This Part II plans duality with p-torsion coefficients in every dimension, following Zavyalov, 'Mod-p Poincaré Duality in p-adic analytic geometry' (Ann. of Math. 201 (2025), 647–773; arXiv:2111.01830v3). Its first prerequisite is ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology.

Final theorems, as the paper states them. Theorem 1.1.4 = 5.4.4: let X be a smooth proper rigid-analytic space of pure dimension d over a non-archimedean field K of mixed characteristic (0, p); there is a Galois-equivariant trace t_X : H^{2d}_ét(X_K̂̄, F_p(d)) → F_p such that H^i_ét(X_K̂̄, F_p) ⊗ H^{2d−i}_ét(X_K̂̄, F_p(d)) → H^{2d}_ét(X_K̂̄, F_p(d)) → F_p is perfect for every i ≥ 0. Theorem 5.4.2: t_X is an isomorphism when X is geometrically connected. Theorem 5.4.5: the same for an étale F_p-local system L paired with L^∨(d). Theorems 5.5.2, 5.5.4, 5.5.6: the derived pairings RΓ_ét(X_C, Λ) ⊗^L RΓ_ét(X_C, Λ(d)) → Λ are perfect and Galois-equivariant for Λ = Z/p^n, Z_p (t_{X,Z_p} = lim t_{X,Z/p^n}) and Q_p. Theorem 5.1.1 = 5.2.4 and Theorem 5.2.5: for X smooth proper over C = K̂̄ there is a global trace Tr_X : RΓ(X, O^{+,a}/p) → O^a_C/p(−d)[−2d], independent of the model, whose cup-product pairing is almost perfect, derived and in each degree. Theorem 4.4.24 = 4.1.2 (local almost duality): for a nice admissible formal O_C-scheme 𝔛 (separated, smooth generic fibre of pure dimension d, reduced special fibre), Faltings' pairing Rν_∗(O^{+,a}/p) ⊗^L Rν_∗(O^{+,a}/p) → Rν_∗(O^{+,a}/p) → ω^{•,a}_{𝔛_0}(−d)[−2d] is almost perfect in D(𝔛_0)^a. Remark 1.1.5 records that no duality holds for ℓ = char K.

Layers, in order. (0) Inputs from Zavyalov's memoir on almost coherent sheaves (Mem. EMS 19, 2025): almost coherent modules and sheaves on admissible formal O_C-schemes, D_acoh(𝔛)^a, RalHom, almost coherence of proper pushforward, almost Grothendieck duality for proper O_C/p-schemes, and Rν_∗(O^{+,a}/p) ∈ D^{[0,d]}_acoh(𝔛_0)^a, Rν_∗Ô^{+,a} ∈ D^{[0,d]}_acoh(𝔛)^a; build them on the abstract almost category of PerfectoidSpaces P0. (1) Duality on formal schemes (§§2.4–2.7): ω^•_𝔛 = R lim ω^•_{𝔛_n} and ω_𝔛 (Theorem 2.4.4, Corollary 2.4.5, Lemmas 2.4.6–2.4.8, Corollary 2.4.9); the Hartogs-type extension ω_𝔛 ≅ j_{𝔘,∗}(ω_𝔛|_𝔘) ∩ (ω_𝔛)_K for smooth generic and geometrically reduced special fibre (Lemmas 2.5.3–2.5.4, Theorem 2.5.5); traces of proper maps of models (Lemmas 2.6.1–2.6.2); s_𝔛 : Ω^d_{X_K} ≅ (ω_𝔛)_K and the coherent trace f_∗Ω^d_X → Ω^d_Y for proper smooth rigid spaces (Lemmas 2.7.3, 2.7.5, Theorem/Definition 2.7.6, Lemma 2.7.9), with Appendix C (generic fibres of O_𝔛-modules, Lemmas C.4–C.9). (2) Faltings' trace (§3): R̃^nν_∗Ô^+ and the BMS maps Φ^n for arbitrary admissible 𝔛 (Definitions 3.2.1, 3.2.5, Lemmas 3.2.2–3.2.4); Ψ on smooth models (Lemmas 3.3.1–3.3.2, Theorem/Definition 3.3.4); Scholze's map on tori and its comparison with Φ^n on the generic fibre (Lemmas 3.4.5, 3.4.7–3.4.8, Corollary 3.4.9, Theorem 3.4.12, Definitions 3.4.13–3.4.14); Tr^{d,+}_{F,𝔛} (Theorem 3.5.2), the integral and mod p Faltings traces (Definitions 3.5.3, 3.5.5, Lemma 3.5.4); pseudo-finite maps and the compatibilities (Lemmas 3.6.4, 3.6.6, Corollary 3.6.5), with the pro-étale traces of Appendix D. (3) Polystable models (§4.2): Definitions 4.2.1–4.2.2, dualizing complexes (Lemmas 4.2.5, 4.2.7), the standard Z_p(1)^d-cover and its perfectoidness (Lemmas 4.2.8, 4.2.11, 4.2.13), the character decomposition and continuous cohomology (Lemma 4.2.23, Corollaries 4.2.25–4.2.26), Lη_{1−ζ_p} (Lemma 4.2.27, Corollaries 4.2.28–4.2.29) and Theorem 4.2.30, t^+_𝔛 : R^dν_∗Ô^+/[1 − ζ_p] ≅ ω_𝔛(−d). (4) Local duality on polystable models (§4.3): Theorem 4.3.2 for F_p[t_0..t_n]/(t_0⋯t_n), Proposition 4.3.6, Lemma 4.3.10 (duality for continuous cohomology of Z_p^d), Theorems 4.3.15–4.3.16, Corollary 4.3.17. (5) Descent (§4.4): the local altered uniformization theorem (Zavyalov, Israel J. Math. 263, 2024, Theorem 1.4) and quotients by finite groups (Zavyalov, Algebra Number Theory 18, 2024) as inputs; rig-isomorphisms (Lemma 4.4.3); equivariant modules and homotopy (co)invariants, almost versions, Lemmas 4.4.11, 4.4.15, 4.4.19, 4.4.21–4.4.23; Theorem 4.4.24. (6) Global duality and the étale theorems (§5): Definitions 5.2.1, 5.2.3, Lemma 5.2.2, Theorems 5.2.4–5.2.5, 5.4.2, Lemma 5.4.3, Theorems 5.4.4–5.4.5, Lemma 5.5.1, Theorems 5.5.2, 5.5.4, 5.5.6.

Import, never re-plan: ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H0 and H3 (classical étale sheaves, Rf_!, finite étale traces; with this paper's source route, Berkovich's trace t_f for smooth partially proper morphisms and all torsion coefficients, Theorem 5.3.3, and the étale Huber–Berkovich comparison of Appendix A); Six-functor formalisms and analytic stacks (AnalyticStacks) AS.1 (with this paper's source route, Grothendieck duality for universally coherent schemes, §§2.2–2.3: f^!, relative dualizing complexes, ω_X and its reflexivity); Adic coefficients and comparison with schemes (AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons) L2 (finitely presented compactifications, §2.1); Adic Spaces PartII (AdicSpacesPartII) R2, R3, F0 (admissible formal schemes, finite traces, Lütkebohmert–Temkin, and via the source route the Reduced Fibre Theorem, Elkik's algebraization and Appendix B); Berkovich spaces, tropical curves and nonarchimedean arithmetic (TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic) TB.0; P-adic Hodge theory and geometric comparison (PadicHodgeTheory) P8 (Scholze's primitive comparison, finiteness and Ω^n(−n) ≅ R^nµ_∗Ô); Integral A_inf cohomology and Breuil–Kisin–Fargues structures (AInfCohomology) AI.0 (Breuil–Kisin twists, Fontaine's theorem on dlog), AI.1 (Lη), AI.3 (the toric perfectoid cover), AI.4 (BMS Theorem 8.3) and AI.6 (the semistable local analysis of Česnavičius–Koshikawa, which §4.2 extends to polystable models; reuse it where the scopes agree); Perfectoid rings and spaces (PerfectoidSpaces) P0, P3; Perfectoid quotients and their prismatic prerequisites (PerfectoidQuotients) Q0; Analytic adic geometry required for diamonds (AdicEtaleGeometry) A1, A2; Derived de Rham cohomology and its algebraic foundations (DerivedDeRhamCohomology) DD.0; Global Galois duality and compact coefficients (ArithmeticGaloisDuality) D7. Prerequisites: Zavyalov's three papers above, Scholze's 'p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties' with its corrigendum, Berkovich's 'Étale cohomology for non-Archimedean analytic spaces', Bosch–Lütkebohmert–Raynaud IV. Tests: the torus T^d (Lemma 3.4.7), the Tate curve or a smooth proper curve with semistable reduction (Faltings' trace against the residue trace), the model O_C⟨t_0, t_1⟩/(t_0t_1 − ϖ) with ϖ ∈ 𝔪 (Warning 4.2.22: R^+_χ not flat) and P^1 (t_X an isomorphism).
routes.reason: ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology plans Huber's classical cohomology of rigid spaces, including traces and Poincaré duality (H3), but only with torsion prime to p and only for curves; no layer plans duality for p-torsion étale cohomology of rigid spaces, Faltings' trace or almost duality on formal models. These extend that roadmap's direction, so they form its Part II. It imports p-adic Hodge theory (P8, AI.0–AI.6) rather than re-planning it, and nothing it builds is used by those layers.

AS.1 owns the quasi-coherent Grothendieck duality formalism (PAPER-BHATT-ETAL-23 and PAPER-HACON-WITASZEK-23 route their singular coherent-duality adapters there). Zavyalov's §2.2 extends the Stacks Project's f^! from noetherian to universally coherent bases, which is what duality over a rank-one valuation ring and over O_C/p needs: Theorems 2.2.2–2.2.3, base change, smooth and étale cases, the relative dualizing complex and its amplitude. §2.3's depth argument that ω_X is reflexive over such a ring belongs with it.

L2 plans noetherian approximation and the nonnoetherian Nagata compactification theorem for qcqs schemes. Zavyalov's §2.1 adds the category of finitely presented compactifications, its behaviour under limits of bases and its cofilteredness with strict morphisms, which the upper-shriek construction needs.

R2 plans admissible formal schemes, admissible blow-ups and the generic-fibre functor, and F0 the formal geometry compared with generic fibres (properness and separatedness via models, algebraization). The facts of Appendix B and Theorem 2.7.1 are statements of that theory: dimension of models, Elkik's algebraization with pure relative dimension, A = A°_K for reduced special fibre, the finite Reduced Fibre Theorem with its universal property, and the localization of reduced-fibre models at rig-isomorphisms.

H3 owns traces and Poincaré duality in Huber's theory (PAPER-GUO-REINECKE-24 routes the Berkovich–Zavyalov trace here). §5.3 and Appendix A translate Berkovich's trace for smooth partially proper morphisms, for all torsion coefficients, into adic language through Huber's comparison of étale topoi (Theorem A.15, overconvergent sheaves, Lemma A.19); Huber's and Berkovich's ℓ-adic duality in all dimensions (Theorem 1.1.3) is the general form of H3's curve case.

TB.0 plans Berkovich spaces and their comparison with Huber's adic spectra. Appendix A needs the global form: Huber's equivalence between Hausdorff strictly analytic Berkovich spaces and taut adic spaces locally of finite type, and how partially proper, proper, étale and smooth morphisms correspond to boundaryless, proper, quasi-étale and quasi-smooth ones.

P8 owns the relative period sheaves and their proper-smooth comparison on rigid spaces, and PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-18 routes Scholze's finiteness theorem for proper smooth rigid spaces here. The paper consumes three more theorems of the same paper of Scholze: the primitive comparison, the agreement of pro-étale and étale cohomology for F_p and O^+/p, and Ω^n_X(−n) ≅ R^nµ_∗Ô_X with coherence.

AI.0 constructs Breuil–Kisin twists, distinguishing A_inf{1}, its étale realization Z_p(1) and O_C{1}. Fontaine's theorem that dlog identifies O_C(1) with (ζ_p − 1)O_C{1} (reproved as Theorem 3.3.3) and Bhatt's computations L̂_{O_C/Z_p} ≅ O_C{1}[1], L̂_{perfectoid/O_C} = 0 are the facts about that twist the paper uses.
